physicalEvidence.summary: Full Adaptive Robotic Information Gathering paper §5.3 deploys a Clearpath autonomous surface vehicle with downward sonar and onboard computation in an 80×88 m quarry-lake area. Learned neural-network-parametrized Attentive Kernel uncertainty selects informative waypoints; conventional PD tracking executes linear/angular velocity commands. This is an actual closed-loop adaptive mapping experiment, not just bathymetric data replay. It is a 2023 study published in the 2024 journal issue, co-advised with Lantao Liu; current independent apparatus and visitor access are not verified, so physical20.

unknowns: Host is Indiana University Bloomington, not Indianapolis or former Tufts. Public contact is rkhardon@iu.edu. The faculty homepage warns of fake research offers using non-IU addresses; do not treat such messages as verified recruitment.

The 2024 POAM work concerns online probabilistic mapping and does not supply an independently verified new physical deployment here. The October 2025 temporally extended MBRL paper uses simulated environments, including MuJoCo locomotion, not new physical robot trials.

The 2025 method learns transition/reward models and plans with them, rather than learning a deployed policy directly. Neural-kernel mapping is learned estimation guiding planning; low-level ASV tracking remains conventional.
